items.title: Thinking Machines details Inkling 2 Small trained with a native 4-bit forward pass from first pretraining step through RL
items.summary: A write-up of how Inkling 2 Small was trained with a 4-bit (NVFP4) forward pass and MXFP8 gradients on GB300s, with the stated result of pretraining in 68 hours. Repliers cite about 8% faster pretraining and 20% faster RL than full MXFP8 at roughly 2% lower compute efficiency, which a builder training low-precision models can check against the post.

reception.summary: Repliers mostly praise it; a few restate the speed and efficiency numbers and note only the forward pass is 4-bit.

items.title: Google Antigravity adds Dynamic Workflows: the agent writes a Python script to orchestrate subagents
items.summary: The /run-workflow command has the agent write a reviewable Python script that runs parallel and sequential subagents with structured handoffs, aiming for deterministic control flow instead of prompt drift. Repliers say the script can be read and re-run before it executes.

doubt.pushback: No link or docs in the post; replies ask how failures and permissions are handled.

reception.summary: Repliers like the script-as-orchestration idea and ask about failure handling and tool permissions; one cancelled over the weekly quota timer, unrelated to the feature.

items.title: Claude Code Projects coordinator now answers in project chat and reports on thread status
items.summary: In a Claude Code project, the coordinator that runs tasks across parallel threads is more proactive: it answers questions in the project chat and posts updates on the status of ongoing threads.

doubt.pushback: Some repliers still lack access or report repeated permission prompts and fast usage drain.

reception.summary: Some say it fixes tab-hopping; others report no access yet, constant approval prompts and quota burn.

items.title: NVIDIA announces GR00T 2, an open robotics System One model that transfers skills across robot bodies
items.summary: GR00T 2 is described as an open model that learns skills from human demonstrations and predicts how its actions change the world, with skills carrying across robot bodies. The post shows a demo video and gives no weights or paper link.

doubt.pushback: Nothing to check in the post itself: no weights, paper or numbers linked.

reception.summary: Replies are mostly off-topic comments about NVIDIA leadership; the few on topic praise the chore demo and nobody reports trying it.

items.title: Independent vision benchmark compares Gemini 4 Hydrogen with Argon and Carbon on cost and speed
items.summary: A long thread runs Gemini 4 Hydrogen against Argon and Carbon on detection, text reading and extraction tasks. At high effort Hydrogen averages 29.3 s per image versus 51.4 for Argon and 132.3 for Carbon at about $0.0379 per image, and at low effort Argon is the pick on price.

items.title: Artificial Analysis Controlled Voice Arena: Speechify Simba 3.5 ranks #1, level with HeyGen Voice
items.summary: Simba 3.5 takes first place in the Controlled Voice arena, statistically level with HeyGen Voice and ahead of Qwen-Audio-3.1-TTS-Plus at 1176, and is fifth on Provider Voice, level with Cartesia Sonic.

items.title: Artificial Analysis launches the Diarization Index benchmark for who-said-what in speech to text
items.summary: A new benchmark scores speech-to-text APIs on Word Diarization Error Rate, the share of words given to the wrong speaker or none, across 97 conversations of two or more speakers.

items.title: MiniMax H3-Image becomes the top open-weights image model on Artificial Analysis editing and text-to-image
items.summary: H3-Image is #1 among open-weights models on both AA-Image-Editing v2.1 and AA-Image-T2I v2.1, ranking #13 overall in editing and #25 in text to image. A faster Highspeed variant is API only.

items.title: vstack agentic formal verification turns up rare-combination bugs in vLLM
items.summary: Hao AI Lab applied its vstack tool to vLLM with the project's team and lists bugs found in rare feature combinations, including zero-cache continuation, a queue-limit lockout, a shared-cache out-of-bounds write, stale LoRA weights after in-place reload and cross-image cache mix-ups, with fixes going upstream.

doubt.pushback: Thread lists the bug classes but links no issues or patches yet.

items.title: browser-use 1.0.4 raises prompt cache hit rate from 78% to 96%, cutting cost per task by a third
items.summary: After a harness fix, cache hits go from 78% to 96%, cost per task falls from $0.67 to $0.45 and time from 5.0 to 4.6 minutes at the same eval score. Available as browser-use 1.0.4.

items.title: browser-use adds 1Password login so agents can sign in without seeing the password
items.summary: An agent that hits a login page asks the user to approve in 1Password, which fills the credentials while the agent never sees the password and keeps going.

doubt.pushback: Demo video only; nothing independent to check.

items.title: NVIDIA Deja View interactive demo opens on Hugging Face with no code needed
items.summary: An interactive Space lets anyone try NVIDIA's Deja View model in the browser without writing code.

doubt.pushback: Post does not say what the model does.

items.title: Baseten open-sources a Rust and CUDA inference engine for DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
items.summary: A from-scratch engine reports about 1,740 tok/s decode on 4xB300 and 2,060 on 8xB300, with a 1M-token prefill in about 12 seconds.

doubt.pushback: Vendor-run numbers; the repo link was not resolvable from the post.

security_na.reason: vLLM bugs (cache OOB write, lockout) found by formal verification; vLLM is not in stack.json and is not agent tooling, supply chain or containers.
